prompt_a: In internal/datacoord/snapshot_manager.go, raise snapshotPinCleanupTimeout from 5 seconds to 20 seconds. The reason, which you know and nobody else working on this code does: on the Ostrava deployment, whose etcd spans three availability zones about 40 ms apart, releasing the pins of a large snapshot takes 6 to 9 seconds, so the cleanup was cancelled at 5 seconds and the pins stayed until the next restart, holding segments the garbage collector should have freed.
prompt_b: snapshotPinCleanupTimeout in internal/datacoord/snapshot_manager.go is 20 seconds. Someone points out that releasing pins normally finishes in well under a second and wants 5 seconds again so a stuck etcd fails quickly. Is that safe? Recommend, and explain what decides the value.
reason: On the Ostrava deployment (etcd across three zones ~40 ms apart) releasing a large snapshot's pins takes 6-9 s, so a 5 s timeout leaked the pins until restart.
key: Not safe: on the Ostrava deployment, whose etcd spans three availability zones about 40 ms apart, releasing a large snapshot's pins takes 6 to 9 seconds; at 5 seconds the cleanup was cancelled and the pins stayed until the next restart, holding segments the garbage collector should have freed.
